source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Start closer INR monitoring because antibiotics can alter warfarin effect and bleeding risk","B":"Continue warfarin unchanged without added INR checks because antibiotics do not interact","C":"Double the warfarin dose during antibiotic therapy to prevent inadequate anticoagulation","D":"Automatically stop warfarin for every antibiotic course regardless of INR or indication"}}
source_row.rationale: Antibiotics and the infection itself can alter warfarin response, and specific anti-infectives may raise or lower INR through different mechanisms. The safe response is closer INR and bleeding/thrombosis monitoring with dose adjustment based on measured response rather than assuming a uniform direction of interaction.
source_row.source_detail: Drug interactions/monitoring: interacting anti-infectives may alter anticoagulant response; INR should be monitored more closely when interacting drugs are started or stopped; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: A client stable on warfarin starts an antibiotic. What is the safest nursing expectation regarding anticoagulation monitoring?
